Each model's capabilities object also includes thinking.types.between_tools, which reports whether the model accepts thinking: {type: "between_tools"}, the setting that turns off up-front thinking. supported is false when the model rejects "between_tools" with a 400 error. Even when supported is true, the API can still reject a "between_tools" request for another reason, such as an effort level that the model doesn't allow with "between_tools". For Claude Sonnet 5.5, for example, the Models API reports thinking.types.between_tools.supported as true and thinking.types.disabled.supported as false.

Code written for Claude Haiku 4.5 can break on Claude Haiku 5.5. Manual extended thinking (budget_tokens), the sampling parameters temperature, top_p, and top_k, and assistant message prefill can each return a 400 error. computer_20250124 also returns a 400 error: use the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset on the Claude API and Google Cloud, or computer_20251124 on Amazon Bedrock. A request that sends thinking blocks back after a change to system, tools, or earlier turns can also return a 400 error. Adaptive thinking is on by default, so a response can begin with thinking blocks, and their text is omitted unless you set thinking.display to "summarized". The same text also counts as more tokens. See the migration guide for each change. For model-specific prompting patterns, see Prompting Claude Haiku 5.5.

For each document included in a request, Rerank combines the tokens from the query with the tokens from the document and the combined total counts toward the context limit for a single document. If the combined number of tokens from the query and a given document exceeds the model’s context length for a single document, the document will automatically get chunked and processed in multiple inferences. See our best practice guide for more info about formatting documents for the Rerank endpoint.

Rerank 5 is our latest generation, available in two tiers: Pro for the highest ranking quality, and Fast for latency- and cost-sensitive workloads. Both support Context Focus, which returns the most relevant passages within each document in the same call, and calibrated relevance scores, which let you set one threshold across queries and domains.

Rerank is the fastest way to inject the intelligence of a language model into an existing search system. Rerank 5, available in Pro and Fast, is our latest generation and adds Context Focus, which returns the most relevant passages within each document. It can be accessed via the Rerank endpoint.

Rerank models sort documents by their relevance to a query. They sit on top of an existing keyword, vector, or hybrid search system and reorder its results so the most relevant come first, with no re-indexing required.
